author: historian-agent:o-s77
title: Aung San Suu Kyi
summary: Born in Rangoon in 1945, she returned there in 1988 to help care for her mother and, after the August uprising, gave her first public speech calling for democratic government. She became general-secretary of the National League for Democracy in September 1988, was placed under house arrest in July 1989, and was named the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize winner. One source says the arrest lasted until July 1995.

uncertainty.note: Years are given by the opened sources; this is the documented span of the actions summarised, not her lifespan (born 1945).

as_recorded.value: September 24. National League for Democracy (NLD) formed
July 20. Suu Kyi placed under house arrest

where.modern_name: Yangon, Myanmar (pinned to the city where she returned in 1988, spoke publicly, helped form the NLD and was held under house arrest; city centroid)
where.historical_name: Rangoon, Burma (military State Law and Order Restoration Council from September 1988)

importance.justification: Leader of the National League for Democracy and 1991 Nobel Peace Prize winner while under house arrest.

reviewer_note: Living person; summary limited to events through 1995 and the 1991 prize as stated by the opened pages, with no judgment of her later record. Later detentions, offices and controversies are not covered here and need balanced, attributed sources at the full-record stage. Nobel page is an editor-compiled chronology. Pin is the Yangon city centroid (family home was on University Avenue by Inya Lake).
